matches.quote: Scan disorder strength and type: dense Gaussian, dilute strong (unitary) scatterers, smooth out-of-plane dopant potentials, hopping disorder, and surface-localized versus bulk disorder.
The miscut tolerance of the Laue-based alignment is not stated. A vicinal surface would contain (100)/(010) micro-facets that carry no flat band.
A single Gaussian onsite disorder strength (σ = 100 meV...) is shown... There is no scan in σ, no disorder averaging
The Fig. 3 caption states Δk = 0.2 Å⁻¹... whereas the text and Methods give about 0.4 Å⁻¹... The authors also state that the simulation overestimates k_z broadening.
The lateral correlation of the roughness is unknown, since it lies below AFM resolution. The authors concede that sub-nm lateral roughness could destroy the states.
A single Gaussian onsite disorder strength (σ = 100 meV...) is shown, apparently for a single realization. There is no scan in σ, no disorder averaging
Scan disorder strength and type: dense Gaussian, dilute strong (unitary) scatterers, smooth out-of-plane dopant potentials, hopping disorder, and surface-localized versus bulk disorder.
The doping estimate does not rule out a non-superconducting surface... with values up to p ≈ 0.3 for alternative fits. This upper range lies beyond the superconducting dome
The surface doping estimate (p ≈ 0.227) comes from fits the authors themselves describe as distorted and imperfect... the tight-binding chemical potential was tuned to match the nodal k_F
'Pristine' surface is asserted rather than established... There is no in situ LEED, core-level XPS, cross-sectional TEM of the cleave

notes: C11 and C14 are judged 'partly' because Section 4.3 of the review explicitly recommends scanning smooth out-of-plane dopant potentials and surface-localized versus bulk disorder (linked to the disorder-modeling critique in P3), without detailing the inter-chirality scattering or surface projection mechanisms. C6 is 'partly' (P7) because the review critiques the inconsistent k_z broadening in the simulations and its effect on feature visibility, whereas C5 (nodal-antinodal gap mixing via k_z broadening) is not specifically proposed.
